hypothesis: An independent veto gate can reduce M1 two-hit premature and normal alarms while preserving effective recall and all fulltext outputs.
score: M1 p_binary[1]; gate only affects temporal alarms
primary_alarm_policy: p_prev>=0.5 AND p_current>=0.5 AND sigmoid(gate)>=0.5; k1 remains the M1 diagnostic policy

pair_data.normal_rule: up to 4 unique adjacent pairs per call: current turn 2 and final turn, plus 2 seeded random remaining turns
pair_data.fraud_pre_rule: up to 2 unique pairs with current<tE: current tE-1 prioritized then one seeded random remaining turn
pair_data.fraud_post_rule: up to 2 unique pairs with current>=tE: current max(2,tE) prioritized then final turn
pair_data.weak_supervision_note: normal call labels and tE boundary are projected mechanically; not independent blind prefix labels

features.scaler: Train-only group-weighted mean/std; std<1e-6 becomes1; z-score clipped to [-8,8]
features.weight_rule: group mass / scenarios in group / calls in scenario / pairs in call; random shuffle with mean-one sample-weighted BCE

gate_architecture: Linear(10,16), Tanh, Linear(16,1), no dropout; torch seed202 initial first layer, last weight0 biaslog(9)
optimizer: AdamW; all20 epochs, use final epoch only; no Dev checkpoint selection

status_rules.hold: noninferiority passes but any improvement failure

selection_policy: one fixed run; no Dev selection of weight/threshold/epoch/features
test_policy: never read or evaluate V365 Test/restricted labels
